If you're not interested in reading a nerd's ramblings, scroll down right to the bottom of this post.

Okay, you want flairs to show up on the right side instead of the left side? No problem, TSG's got ya covered.

Do take note, however, that this is somewhat hacky and requires CSS changes every single time you add a new flair. However, it has the bonus of working on more older browsers (I'm pretty sure it won't work for all, but whatever yolo).

So, we have a flair that is labeled "5-10 minutes".

No problem.

Here's the relevant HTML code just to help understand what's going on. If you don't care or don't understand it or don't need this, feel free to scroll down past this code block.

<span class="flair 5-10-m" title="5-10 mins">
 5-10 mins
</span>
<a class="title may-blank " title="(title)" tabindex="1" href="(url)">
 (title)
</a>

Now in this case, my flair class is called 5-10-m. Now you'll notice immediately after, you have an <a> element, which is used for making links -- and it also happens to be the title. Great, so we want to put the flair after the title.

First of all, I'm working with the assumption that you want every flair to go after the title. If you don't, please let me know.

Anyway, make the flair invisible. 

.flair{
display:none;
}

Why? Because you can't move it. We want the flair to go after the title, so here's what we shall do, we shall create a pseudo-element that looks identical to the flair after the title. 

.flair+a.title:after{

}

This block will select the title element immediately after the flair element. The + will select any element immediately after a .flair element. Why is it necessary to have .flair there at all, surely it would be more efficient to simply have a.title:after? Well, not every submission will have a flair. Thus, it is necessary to only select submissions which have flair to be eligible for a post-flair. The :after selector creates a fake element immediately after the title.

Next we want to actually create that flair! I will merely lift the actual flair code out. I've also made the font-weight less because otherwise the flair'd be bold, and I've added a 3px margin to the left side so it doesn't glue itself to the title.

.flair+a.title:after{
font-size: x-small;
margin-top: -1px;
background: #F8F8F8;
border: 1px solid #E6E6E6;
border-radius: 2px;
color: #666;
line-height: 150%;
margin-right: 3px;
padding: 2px 4px;
vertical-align: middle;
display:inline-block;
font-weight:400;
margin-left:3px;
}

IMPORTANT NOTICE: DO NOT USE NUMBERS IN YOUR FLAIR CLASS

It's a CSS bug that I forgot about. Good work CSS.

Finally, we want to make sure they have an actual label. Just create the following block:

.flair.test+a.title:after{
content:"5-10 minutes"
}

This looks similar to the above selector, but this time it only selects titles that come after the flair with a class of test, and it gives them the label "5-10 minutes". If you have more than one flair, you will obviously need to repeat this process with every single level of flair.

Example:

.flair.test+a.title:after{
content:"5-10 minutes"
}
.flair.test-two+a.title:after{
content:"10-15 minutes"
}
.flair.test-three+a.title:after{
content:"15-20 minutes"
}

Though obviously you will need to select the flair CSS classes that you yourself have specified in your flair settings. I only used test as an example, because that's the class I used when I was testing.

You can see a working example in /v/tsg2.

Anyway I wish you luck on your sub. I might actually go there often, it's a really great idea!

Anyway here's all the code. It's actually quite a short solution!

.flair{
display:none;
}
.flair+a.title:after{
font-size: x-small;
margin-top: -1px;
background: #F8F8F8;
border: 1px solid #E6E6E6;
border-radius: 2px;
color: #666;
line-height: 150%;
margin-right: 3px;
padding: 2px 4px;
vertical-align: middle;
display:inline-block;
font-weight:400;
margin-left:3px;
}
.flair.test+a.title:after{
content:"5-10 minutes";
}
.flair.test-two+a.title:after{
content:"10-15 minutes";
}
.flair.test-three+a.title:after{
content:"15-20 minutes";
}

It works! Thank you.

7.Nf3 Bd6
